findings: - warning .github/workflows/pstack-drift.yml:17 the weekly run is unproven on the runner: the expression reads `github.event.repository.private`, the only drift runs so far are `workflow_dispatch` ones, and if a `schedule` event carries no `repository` the job goes to `ubuntu-latest` and does not start while the minutes are out. The test models `private` as a boolean and cannot see it. Either read the runner name of the first scheduled run after the merge, or pick by a source that is there on every event (both reviewers)

- warning .github/workflows/check.yml:18 the comment says a public repo "never" runs here, and the line cannot hold that: on `pull_request` GitHub reads the workflow from the pull request's own commit, so in a public repo a fork can write `runs-on: [self-hosted, hydra]` while the runner is registered. Say only what the line does (the repo's own jobs leave the runner once it is public), and that taking the runner's registration away is what keeps a stranger off this machine (both reviewers)

- warning .github/workflows/pstack-drift.yml:17 on this runner `make pstack-drift` keeps its clone in the user's real `~/.cache/hydra/cursor-plugins` (`src/pdrift/cli.py:64`), outside the workspace `actions/checkout` cleans: it outlives the job, is shared with the user's own `make pstack-drift`, and a clone cut off by the 10 minute limit leaves a `.git` every later run reuses. `XDG_CACHE_HOME: ${{ runner.temp }}` on that step keeps it inside the job

- info tests/test_workflows.py:100 `PICK.fullmatch` already pins the expression character for character, so `runner` and `runners` evaluate nothing GitHub evaluates: comparing `jobs(text)` with the one expected expression per file checks the same and drops the regex, both helpers and the `json` import
- info .github/workflows/pstack-drift.yml:15 the copied comment gives "a stranger's pull request" as the reason on a workflow only `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` can start (both reviewers)
dismissed: - a job with no `runs-on` makes the test raise `TypeError`, not fail an assertion: it still fails loud, and no such job exists
- two `Done when` lines have no evidence in the diff: the evidence is the runs, and the proof read them at this head
answers: Finding: not fixed, the weekly run is unproven on the runner for a schedule event, because the brief's Done when fixes the fact to `github.event.repository.private`, a schedule runs only from the default branch so no run on this branch can prove it, and the reviewer's other remedy is a look after the merge, which is under Noticed for the home
Finding: fixed, the comment said a public repo never runs here; it now says the repo's own jobs leave the runner and that removing the runner's registration is what keeps a stranger off
Finding: fixed, the drift clone outlived the job in the user's cache; the step sets `XDG_CACHE_HOME: ${{ runner.temp }}`, and run 38292420468 passed on `the user-hydra` with it at `_work/_temp`
Finding: fixed, the test's regex and two helpers evaluated nothing; it compares each job's `runs-on` with the one expected expression
Finding: fixed, the drift workflow's comment gave a stranger's pull request as its reason; it no longer does

A2.why: schedule event may carry no repository, weekly run unproven

A3.why: drift clone in the user's real ~/.cache outlives the job

A4.why: uv cache and tool install persist outside the workspace; in no Review line

A5.why: job with no runs-on raises TypeError; its *.yml glob half is the noted .yaml issue

A6.why: copied comment names a stranger's pull request on a schedule/dispatch workflow

A7.why: Done when line 3 has no evidence in the diff

B1.why: weekly pstack-drift run probably still picks ubuntu-latest

B2.why: 'never' rule lives in a file a pull request can rewrite

B3.why: PICK/runner/runners layer evaluates nothing; compare with one expected expression

B4.why: glob misses .yaml workflows; in no Review line

B5.why: copied comment describes a trigger the workflow lacks

B6.why: two Done when lines have no evidence in the diff (also touches uv cache, the noted issue)
